item.title: Deconstructing Nodejs require(): Browser Incompatibility and Module Loading Mechanics
item.description:
“Deconstructing Nodejs require(): Browser Incompatibility and Module Loading Mechanics”

The introduction of modularity into JavaScript applications—breaking large codebases into isolated files—is fundamental to modern development. In the Node.js server environment, the mechanism for achieving this is heavily reliant on require(), module.exports, and exports.

The Core Role of require() in Node.js

In a Node.js context, require() is a built-in function specifically designed to load and cache external JavaScript modules. This mechanism is defined by the CommonJS specification .

item.title: Resolving Node.js 'Cannot use import statement outside a module' Syntax Error
item.description:
“Resolving Node.js ‘Cannot use import statement outside a module’ Syntax Error”

Encountering the SyntaxError: Cannot use import statement outside a module in a Node.js context signals a conflict between the required JavaScript module system (ES Modules, or ESM) and the environment’s default interpretation (typically CommonJS, or CJS). This situation arises when using the modern import/export syntax in files that Node.js expects to be CJS modules.

What are the robust methods to configure a Node.js project to correctly handle ECMAScript Module (import/export) syntax?
